Recipes — views, datasets and apps to copy

Finished, tested recipes to copy into Report Studio or Plugin Studio — fleet KPIs, policies without a WAF profile, traffic log off, policies by App ID, certificates expiring before a date, FortiGate policies, FortiADC virtual servers with their pool members, an administrator dataset with a widget, and a script over a dataset field.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsstudio.plugin_studio studio.script_library
📍 WherePlugins → Report Studio → New view; Plugin Studio → New app
On this page
  • 1. Fleet at a glance (widget)
  • 2. Server policies without a WAF profile
  • 3. Policies with the traffic log off
  • 4. Policies grouped by App ID
  • 5. Certificates expiring before a date
  • 6. FortiGate firewall policies (FortiGate ADOM)
  • 7. FortiADC virtual servers and their pool members (FortiADC ADOM)

  • 9. A script over a dataset field

Every recipe lists the datasets to tick and the inputs to add, then the body. They render in SATOM's strict sandbox as written. Report Studio's Browse examples and Plugin Studio's Examples hold more.

1. Fleet at a glance (widget)#

Datasets: fleet_counts, fleet_appliances · Kind: widget

{% set c = fleet_counts.rows[0] if fleet_counts.rows else {"devices": 0, "server_policies": 0, "certificates": 0} %}
<div class="fw-card"><div class="fw-card-body">
  <h3 class="fw-card-title">{{ c.devices }} devices · {{ c.server_policies }} policies · {{ c.certificates }} certificates</h3>
  {% for g in fleet_appliances.rows | groupby("kind") %}
    <span class="fw-badge fw-badge-info">{{ g.grouper or "unknown" }}: {{ g.list | length }}</span>
  {% endfor %}
</div></div>

2. Server policies without a WAF profile#

Datasets: server_policies_full

{% set bare = server_policies_full.rows | rejectattr("wpp") | list %}
<div class="fw-card">
  <div class="fw-card-header"><h2 class="fw-card-title">Policies without a WAF profile — {{ bare | length }} of {{ server_policies_full.rows | length }}</h2></div>
  <div class="fw-card-body">
  {% if bare %}
    <table class="fw-table"><thead><tr><th>Device</th><th>Policy</th><th>Virtual server</th><th>Status</th></tr></thead><tbody>
    {% for p in bare | sort(attribute="device") %}
      <tr><td>{{ p.device }}</td><td><code>{{ p.policy }}</code></td><td>{{ p.vserver }}</td>
          <td><span class="fw-badge {{ 'fw-badge-warning' if p.status == 'enable' else 'fw-badge-secondary' }}">{{ p.status }}</span></td></tr>
    {% endfor %}
    </tbody></table>
  {% else %}<div class="fw-alert fw-alert-success">Every policy has a WAF profile.</div>{% endif %}
  </div>
</div>

3. Policies with the traffic log off#

Datasets: server_policies_full · Input: device (Device, optional)

{% set rows = server_policies_full.rows %}
{% if params.device %}{% set rows = rows | selectattr("appliance_id", "equalto", params.device) | list %}{% endif %}
{% set off = rows | selectattr("traffic_log", "equalto", "disable") | list %}
<p>{{ off | length }} of {{ rows | length }} policies do not log traffic.</p>
<ul>{% for p in off %}<li>{{ p.device }} — <code>{{ p.policy }}</code></li>{% endfor %}</ul>

4. Policies grouped by App ID#

Datasets: server_policies_full (the App ID is parsed from each policy's comment: App ID: APP-1234)

{% for g in server_policies_full.rows | groupby("appid") %}
  <h3>{{ g.grouper or "(no App ID)" }} <span class="fw-badge fw-badge-secondary">{{ g.list | length }}</span></h3>
  <p class="fw-muted">{{ g.list | map(attribute="policy") | join(", ") }}</p>
{% endfor %}

5. Certificates expiring before a date#

Datasets: certificates · Input: before (Date, required)

Dates are ISO text, so comparing text compares dates:

{% set soon = certificates.rows | selectattr("not_after") | list %}
{% set ns = namespace(rows=[]) %}
{% for c in soon | sort(attribute="not_after") %}
  {% if c.not_after[:10] < params.before %}{% set ns.rows = ns.rows + [c] %}{% endif %}
{% endfor %}
<h2>{{ ns.rows | length }} certificate(s) expire before {{ params.before }}</h2>
<table class="fw-table"><thead><tr><th>Name</th><th>Expires</th><th>Status</th></tr></thead><tbody>
{% for c in ns.rows %}<tr><td>{{ c.common_name }}</td><td>{{ c.not_after[:10] }}</td><td>{{ c.status }}</td></tr>{% endfor %}
</tbody></table>

ns.rows + [c] builds a new list: allowed in the immutable sandbox, unlike append.

6. FortiGate firewall policies (FortiGate ADOM)#

Datasets: fortigate_firewall_policy · Input: device (Device, optional)

Device-object datasets give numbers for appliance_id: compare with params.device | int.

{% set rows = fortigate_firewall_policy.rows %}
{% if params.device %}{% set rows = rows | selectattr("appliance_id", "equalto", params.device | int) | list %}{% endif %}
{% set deny = rows | selectattr("action", "equalto", "deny") | list %}
<p>{{ rows | length }} policies · <span class="fw-badge fw-badge-danger">{{ deny | length }} deny</span></p>
<table class="fw-table"><thead><tr><th>Device</th><th>ID</th><th>Name</th><th>Action</th><th>Status</th></tr></thead><tbody>
{% for p in rows | sort(attribute="policyid") %}
<tr><td>{{ p.device }}</td><td>{{ p.policyid }}</td><td>{{ p.name }}</td>
    <td><span class="fw-badge {{ 'fw-badge-success' if p.action == 'accept' else 'fw-badge-danger' }}">{{ p.action }}</span></td>
    <td>{{ p.status }}</td></tr>
{% endfor %}
</tbody></table>

The source and destination interfaces and addresses are sub-objects: fortigate_firewall_policy__srcintf, __dstintf, __srcaddr, __dstaddr (each row's parent_id is its policy's id, its mkey the name).

7. FortiADC virtual servers and their pool members (FortiADC ADOM)#

Datasets: fortiadc_load_balance_virtual_server, fortiadc_load_balance_pool, fortiadc_load_balance_pool__pool_member

<table class="fw-table"><thead><tr><th>Virtual server</th><th>Address</th><th>Port</th><th>Pool</th><th>Members</th></tr></thead><tbody>
{% for vs in fortiadc_load_balance_virtual_server.rows %}
  {% set pools = fortiadc_load_balance_pool.rows | selectattr("mkey", "equalto", vs.pool) | selectattr("appliance_id", "equalto", vs.appliance_id) | list %}
  {% set members = fortiadc_load_balance_pool__pool_member.rows | selectattr("parent_id", "equalto", pools[0].id) | list if pools else [] %}
  <tr><td>{{ vs.mkey }}</td><td>{{ vs.address }}</td><td>{{ vs.port }}</td><td>{{ vs.pool or "—" }}</td>
      <td>{% for m in members %}<code>{{ m.address }}:{{ m.port }}</code> {% endfor %}</td></tr>
{% endfor %}
</tbody></table>

The same pattern works for any object with sub-objects: match the parent on mkey (and the device), then the children on parent_id.

8. An administrator dataset and its widget#

Totals are best computed by SATOM, once, rather than by every view.

  1. An administrator builds, in Administrator → System → Database → Plugin datasets (how): key policies_per_device; base device_server_policies; join appliances (appliance_id → id) and device_objects (object_id → id); filter device_objects.layer = config; columns appliances.name and device_server_policies.name with the aggregate count on the second; it groups by the device name. A plugin reads the columns name and n.
  2. The widget (Datasets: admin_policies_per_device):
{% set rows = admin_policies_per_device.rows | sort(attribute="name") %}
<div class="fw-card"><div class="fw-card-body">
{% for r in rows %}
  <div>{{ r.name }} <span class="fw-badge fw-badge-primary">{{ r.n }}</span></div>
{% else %}
  <p class="fw-muted">No data yet.</p>
{% endfor %}
</div></div>

Values of an administrator dataset arrive as text, so sort(attribute="n") would put "9" after "40". Sort by name, order the rows in the dataset's query, or cast before computing: rows | map(attribute="n") | map("int") | sum.

9. A script over a dataset field#

In the Script Library a form field of type dataset hands the script the rows of a query an author built in the field's Database query panel (the same no-SQL builder), read for the person who runs it.

from satom_script import inputs, result, log

ds = inputs["fleet"]            # {"columns", "rows", "truncated"}; keys are table.col
by_kind = {}
for r in ds["rows"]:
    by_kind[r["appliances.kind"]] = by_kind.get(r["appliances.kind"], 0) + 1
log("%d devices read" % len(ds["rows"]))
result({"devices_by_kind": by_kind, "truncated": ds["truncated"]})
